title: Rain on the Oak
checkpoint: Reception Spring 2, week 1 — Learning — Phase 3: new sounds oa, oo, oo (book)
note_for_grown_ups: Four long-vowel teams arrive here — ai (rain), ee (feet), igh (high) and oa (boat). Each is two or three letters making one long sound; sweep your finger under the whole team as your child says it.

pages.illustration: Pip on a fence rail looking up at a huge green oak in full summer leaf, the tree filling most of the page. Fresh, wet greens.

pages.text: A bug is up high in the oak.
pages.illustration: Close on a single wet leaf high in the oak with a small round beetle on it, its shell shining. Rain-fresh green.

pages.text: It did rain in the night.
pages.illustration: Night scene, seen through a rain-streaked view: the oak dark against a deep blue sky, rain falling in long silver lines. No characters. Atmospheric.

pages.text: The rain fell on a goat.
pages.illustration: Morning after. A goat standing patiently in the field beside the oak, rain still dripping from the branches onto its back.

pages.text: The goat had a wet coat.
pages.illustration: Close on the goat's soaked coat, fur parted into wet points, water beading and running. It looks resigned. Gently funny.

pages.text: Pip sees Ned in a boat.
pages.illustration: Pip on a branch looking down at Ned in a small wooden boat on the pond below. Aerial viewpoint so we see the boat from above.
Ned in the boat with a leaf hoisted as a sail, steering with great concentration towards the reader. The wind is filling the leaf.
Close low view over the side of the boat: Ned's orange webbed feet, clearly visible through the clear shallow water, paddling away. Funny and sweet.

pages.text: We had fun in the rain.
pages.illustration: Closing page: Pip and Ned side by side on the upturned boat on the bank, both dripping wet, a rainbow over the oak behind them. Bright and joyful.
